source.version: arXiv:2604.03529v1 [cs.HC], 4 Apr 2026, as stamped on PDF p. 1; supplied preprint. The citation record identifies a later ICML workshop report, which is not the PDF used for this extraction.
source.supplement_used: Appendices A–C in the same PDF, pp. 18–30; Table 5 on PDF p. 28 supplies the final-story differences and significance markings.

studies.label: Online short-story experiment: AI access crossed with originality versus technical-quality incentives

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1 (recruitment count); PDF p. 5, Table 2 caption (demographic groups); PDF pp. 20 and 25, Appendix A.2 (exclusions not reconciled with those counts)
counts_source.quote: We recruited a total of n “ 200 participants from Prolific, with 50 participants per group.

arms.name: AI-O
arms.description: Integrated gpt5-mini chat assistant with medium reasoning available alongside the editor during writing; prompting at least once required, adoption optional; announced bonus based on originality and uniqueness competition. AI was unavailable during initial brainstorming (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2.1–3.2.2; PDF p. 18, Appendix A.1; PDF p. 20, Appendix A.1.4).

arms.name: SELF-O
arms.description: Write alone in the editor; external AI prohibited; announced bonus based on originality and uniqueness competition. AI was unavailable during initial brainstorming (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2.1–3.2.2; PDF p. 18, Appendix A.1; PDF p. 20, Appendix A.1.4).

arms.name: AI-T
arms.description: Integrated gpt5-mini chat assistant with medium reasoning available alongside the editor during writing; prompting at least once required, adoption optional; announced bonus based on technical-quality grading based on organization and technique. AI was unavailable during initial brainstorming (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2.1–3.2.2; PDF p. 18, Appendix A.1; PDF p. 20, Appendix A.1.4).

arms.name: SELF-T
arms.description: Write alone in the editor; external AI prohibited; announced bonus based on technical-quality grading based on organization and technique. AI was unavailable during initial brainstorming (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2.1–3.2.2; PDF p. 18, Appendix A.1; PDF p. 20, Appendix A.1.4).

studies.task: Write a 250–350-word first-person short story centered on a decision or dilemma and taking place within one day, after an unassisted brainstorming outline (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; PDF p. 20, Appendix A.1.3).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI GPT5-Mini (gpt5-mini with reasoning set to medium)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 1, Introduction; PDF p. 20, Appendix A.1.4. The model release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: OSF: https://osf.io/3u8tq/overview?view_only=e1a8044dd5044bc59dd0a7d8f3fca3c2 (PDF p. 3, footnote 2). PDF p. 5, Section 4, states that all analyses in that section except Figure 1 (right) were preregistered.
preregistration.primary_outcome: Diversity of final stories, assessed with the prespecified embedding and lexical metric suite (PDF p. 6, Section 4.1.1 and Table 3; PDF p. 14, Section 7.2). No single metric is declared the sole preregistered primary.

estimates.notes: Planned AI-access contrast within the originality incentive cell, using the full analyzed cell rather than an adoption subgroup. The reported difference is raw, not a standardized effect. p_value is the unadjusted one-sided bound defined by the black stars, not an exact p-value. The red BH-adjusted marking is ***. Both arm means are printed in the prose at lower precision than the table difference; no difference was recomputed. The Welch tests use one leave-one-out score per participant (PDF pp. 6–7); scores share comparison stories and no adjustment for that dependence is described. No numerical test statistic, degrees of freedom, SD, SE or confidence interval is printed.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: AI-O versus AI-T and SELF-O versus SELF-T, final-story embedding metrics (Table 5 incentive contrasts)
not_extracted.reason: These contrasts change task incentives only. Both AI arms use the same model, reasoning setting and interface; the SELF comparison has no AI arm. The reconciled form codes both as other, which is outside the extraction comparison types; they are not different AI configurations. PDF p. 4, Section 3.2.2; PDF p. 18, Appendix A.1.2; PDF p. 20, Appendix A.1.4; PDF p. 28, Table 5.

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: AI-O versus AI-T and SELF-O versus SELF-T, final-story lexical metrics (Table 5 incentive contrasts)
not_extracted.reason: Incentive-only comparisons with unchanged AI configuration, or two unaided arms. These are coded other in the reconciled form and fall outside ai_vs_bau, ai_vs_active and ai_design. PDF pp. 4, 18, 20; PDF p. 28, Table 5.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: In-progress diversity trajectories, including embedding and lexical robustness plots
not_extracted.reason: The reported between-arm trajectory contrast is AI-O versus AI-T, an incentive-only contrast with the same AI configuration. Figures 2(b) and 16 otherwise display arm trajectories without printed numerical AI-access contrasts or fixed-time arm summaries. They also restrict each time point to sufficiently long drafts; the participating sample at each time is not printed. No values are digitized and no new contrast is constructed from the curves. PDF pp. 8–9, Sections 5.1–5.2 and Figure 2(b); PDF p. 29, Figure 16.

not_extracted.what: S1-O4: First full AI-generated drafts and subsequent AI-draft comparisons, all embedding and lexical metrics
not_extracted.reason: These score assistant-generated drafts rather than the participant-produced final output and do not supply an eligible randomized comparison of human outputs. The First (AI) headings in Table 5 also conflict with the first-draft-minus-final comparison described in Figure 1 and prose. PDF pp. 7–9, Figures 1–2 and Sections 4.2–5.2; PDF p. 28, Table 5.

not_extracted.what: Adoption-stratified final-story embedding similarities (Figure 6 and Table 6)
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup analyses conditional on post-treatment AI-text adoption, not full-sample randomized contrasts. PDF p. 11, Section 6.2; PDF p. 12, Figure 6; PDF p. 28, Appendix C.3; PDF p. 30, Table 6.

not_extracted.what: Adoption-stratified final-story lexical similarities and NGDS (Table 6)
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup analyses conditional on post-treatment AI-text adoption, excluded under the extraction rule for subgroup and mediation-related analyses. PDF p. 28, Appendix C.3; PDF p. 30, Table 6.

not_extracted.what: AI-text adoption/reliance scores, including lexical attribution, embedding attribution and their robustness correlations
not_extracted.reason: These measure how much of a participant’s own final story derives from their AI suggestions, not creativity or diversity across different people. They are process/mechanism outcomes and do not answer the eligible creativity questions. PDF pp. 10–11, Sections 6.1–6.2 and Figure 4(a); PDF pp. 26–27, Appendix B.1 and Figure 14.

not_extracted.what: Time spent brainstorming, writing or prompting; prompt length; number and type of AI requests
not_extracted.reason: Interaction, effort and usage measures rather than creativity or diversity scored on the participant-produced story. PDF pp. 3–5, Sections 3.1–3.3; PDF pp. 10–11, Figures 4–5 and Section 6.2.

not_extracted.what: AI familiarity, self-reported strategies, perceived agency/ownership, satisfaction and attitudes toward AI drafts
not_extracted.reason: Self-reports and attitudes, including perceptions of AI-generated work, are excluded. PDF pp. 12–13, Section 6.3; PDF p. 20, Appendix A.1.5.

not_extracted.what: Qualitative story structure and PCA displays of embedding distributions
not_extracted.reason: Exploratory visualizations of semantic location and illustrative story openings, without a separately defined scalar creativity/diversity outcome or reported randomized between-arm effect. Some panels additionally examine assistant-generated drafts and a subgroup requesting repeated drafts. PDF pp. 8–9, Section 5 and Figure 2(c); PDF p. 29, Figure 17.

not_extracted.what: Individual story creativity, originality and technical-quality ratings
not_extracted.reason: These ratings were not collected or reported as outcomes; the bonus rubric was an incentive manipulation. The paper identifies diversity as its primary outcome and quality as future work, and reports giving a fixed bonus instead of assessing each story. PDF p. 14, Section 7.2; PDF p. 25, Appendix A.4.

open_items: Exact randomized and analyzed people per arm and in total: reconcile recruitment/demographic counts with the exclusions, including any replacement recruitment. PDF p. 3 reports 200 recruited and 50 per group; PDF p. 5 repeats 50 per demographic group; PDF p. 25 reports 29 filtered workers and describes an excluded SELF participant. No subtraction, addition or assumed replacement is used.

Numerically printed arm means are missing for every final-story contrast except MiniLM AI-O versus SELF-O. AI-T’s exact MiniLM level is not stated. Participant-level outcome SDs and arm SEs are also absent. Figures 2(a) and 15 are not digitized.

Diversity-effect SEs, confidence intervals, exact p-values, t statistics and degrees of freedom are not printed. Only significance bounds are recoverable from Table 5. The construction and level of the plotted error bars/bands are unstated.

Compression ratio and NGDS are placed under the general participant-level pairwise framework, but their pairwise implementations are not specified. Obtain the metric definitions/code to resolve this without reclassifying their unit by assumption.
The paper does not give a release year for the named AI model. ai_tool.year is null.

The supplied PDF is the earlier arXiv version; the citation record identifies a later workshop report with different text and formatting. This extraction is specific to the supplied PDF and should not silently be attributed to the later version.

primary_override.question: across_people
primary_override.reason: Apply the codebook tie-breaks: the paper foregrounds all-MiniLM-L12-v2 among the prespecified metric suite. Both AI arms have the same open-chat tool and no combined AI-access contrast is printed. Use the technical-quality incentive cell as the baseline relative to the added originality incentive. This is an extraction tie-break, not a claim that this individual metric/cell was uniquely preregistered as primary.

notes: Extraction completed by A on 2026-10-10. The entire markdown conversion, including references and Appendices A–C, was read in contiguous chunks; every cited PDF page was checked with pymupdf. Table 5 column positions and black/red star colors were checked using PDF text spans. PDF and printed page numbers coincide. Source quotes preserve the PDF text extraction’s math-font glyphs (notably an acute-accent glyph for minus and angle glyphs for stars); numerical fields transcribe their intended printed sign, and the verbatim row quotes preserve printed decimal precision. All extracted effects are raw differences; none were computed from means, figures, stars or other statistics. Star legends supply bounds only. Exact participant counts remain null for the unreconciled flow in the final screening form; the disjoint analyzed adoption groups reported in Table 4 establish eligibility without supplying full-sample counts (PDF p. 13, Table 4; PDF p. 28, Appendix C.3). se_basis is participant because the paper tests one leave-one-out score per person, but these scores share comparisons and the paper describes no dependence correction (PDF pp. 6–7). preregistered_primary=yes refers to the diversity suite, not to a unique metric. No after-AI outcome or individual creativity/quality score was reported. Incentive-only contrasts retain their screening classification outside the specified extraction comparison types. No data, model-only outputs, or post-treatment subgroups were used to fill missing final-story statistics.
